questions: If N is odd and K = floor(N/2), does the unpaired cake simply get ignored, or is there any requirement to use all cakes?

Are we allowed to form pairs arbitrarily, or must we maximize total price? The problem says 'Find the maximum possible total price', so we must compute the optimal pairing, but is there any constraint on which pairs can be formed beyond using each cake at most once?
Does the order of pairs matter? That is, is the total price simply the sum of the prices of each pair, regardless of which pair is considered first?
If two cakes have identical values for all three attributes, are they considered distinct for pairing purposes? (Yes, because they are distinct indices.)
Is it allowed to have K=0? The constraints say 1 ≤ K, so no.
Should the output be a single integer per test case, or could it be large enough to require 64-bit? (Implicitly 64-bit due to values up to 2e9 per pair and K up to 5e4, but not specified.)
Are the pairs independent? That is, does pairing cake A with B affect which other cakes can be paired with each other only through the distinctness constraint, or is there any other interdependence?
If multiple optimal pairings exist, can we output any of their total prices? (Yes, we just need the maximum total price value.)
